Reporting directly to the Manager, Network Inventory, Warehouse Operations and Tool Management, this role bridges strategic network goals and ground-level execution. The Supervisor plays a critical lead role in publishing standardized procedures (DPDs) across all departments and base locations, leading new employee onboarding and training programs, integrating new outbases, driving AMOS system process adoption, and supporting centralized distribution strategies—ensuring full regulatory compliance (CARs, IOSA), high material availability, and process governance.

Duties & Responsibilities:

* **Network-Wide Process Uniformity:** Roll out standardized DPD workflows for receiving, binning, cycle-counting, parts issuing, AOG support, and shipping across primary hubs (YYZ, YTZ, YQT, YAM, YOW, YHZ) and outbases to eliminate local operational variances.
* **Onboarding & Training Standards:** Oversee and facilitate all new employee onboarding, maintaining high training standards and OJT programs across all departments and personnel responsible for material handling to ensure strict compliance with IOSA and Transport Canada regulations.
* **Process Compliance & Auditing:** Perform regular process audits across bases to ensure local stores teams strictly adhere to established DPDs and CARs/IOSA regulatory guidelines.
* **Create & Publish DPDs:** Author, publish, and continuously update all Departmental Process Documents (DPDs) to establish a single, unified operational playbook and ensure standardization across all departments, logistics, and warehouse operations.
* **Outbase Integration:** Project-manage the operational setup and supply chain integration of new outbases and heavy check stations.
* **Systems Integration & Workflow Automation:** Partner with the Manager to translate AMOS and Vertical Lift Module (VLM) operational workflows into standard DPDs, driving network adoption of AMOS APNs to reduce email traffic and automate material requests.

Behavioural Competencies:

* **Concern for Safety:** Identifying hazardous or potentially hazardous situations and taking appropriate action to maintain a safe environment for self and others.
* **Teamwork:** Working collaboratively with others to achieve organizational goals.
* **Passenger/Customer Service:** Providing service excellence to internal and/or external customers (passengers).
* **Initiative:** Dealing with situations and issues proactively and persistently, seizing opportunities that arise.
* **Results Focus:** Focusing efforts on achieving high quality results consistent with the organization’s standards.
* **Fostering Communication:** Listening and communicating openly, honestly, and respectfully with different audiences, promoting dialogue and building consensus.

Qualifications:

* **Experience:** 3+ years of experience in aviation inventory, logistics, or warehouse management, with a strong background in process documentation, workflow design, or multi-site process standardization.
* **Documentation & Writing Skills:** Strong technical writing ability with proven experience creating, publishing, and maintaining formal procedures, SOPs, or Departmental Process Documents (DPDs).
* **Project Leadership:** Track record of leading logistics projects, outbase setup initiatives, or continuous improvement efforts.
* **Technical & Systems Expertise:** Deep familiarity with aviation maintenance software (AMOS experience highly preferred) and automated storage systems (VLM).
* **Regulatory Knowledge:** Solid understanding of Canadian Aviation Regulations (CARs), IOSA standards, and aviation Safety Management Systems (SMS).
* **Education & Credentials:**

Role Summary
  
  
The Head of Operative Medicine leads all surgical and perioperative services across our hospital and ambulatory surgical center in Dubai. The role carries overall accountability for patient safety, clinical quality, surgical outcomes, operating theatre performance and the surgical workforce. The successful candidate will be an internationally trained, board-certified surgeon or anesthesiologist with Western qualifications and senior leadership experience, who will build a high-reliability surgical program aligned with international accreditation standards and Dubai Health Authority (DHA) regulation.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
Clinical Leadership and Quality
  
  

* Provide clinical leadership for all surgical specialties, anesthesia and perioperative care across both sites.
* Establish and monitor surgical quality, safety and outcome indicators, including infection rates, complications, readmissions, unplanned returns to theatre and mortality review.
* Chair or oversee morbidity and mortality reviews, peer review and clinical audit, and ensure learning is acted on.
* Implement evidence-based pathways, including enhanced recovery, WHO surgical safety checklist compliance and VTE prevention.
* Maintain a personal clinical practice at a level agreed with the CEO and CMO.

Operations and Performance
  
  

* Direct operating theatre management, including scheduling, utilization, turnaround, day-case flow and case-mix optimization across the hospital and ambulatory center.
* Define which procedures are suitable for the ambulatory setting, with clear patient selection, escalation and transfer protocols.
* Oversee sterile processing, implant and device management, anesthesia services, recovery and surgical inventory in partnership with supply chain.
* Own the surgical services budget, productivity targets and capital equipment planning.

Medical Staff Governance
  
  

* Lead recruitment, onboarding, credentialing and privileging of surgeons, anesthesiologists and perioperative clinicians in line with DHA requirements.
* Conduct performance and quality review of clinical activity through the established medical staff governance framework, and develop succession plans.
* Foster a just, collaborative culture with strong team communication and psychological safety.

Regulatory, Accreditation and Risk
  
  

* Ensure compliance with DHA regulations, UAE federal health law and Joint Commission International (JCI) or equivalent accreditation standards.
* Lead incident investigation, root cause analysis and risk mitigation for surgical events.
* Maintain readiness for inspections, audits and accreditation surveys.

Strategy and Growth
  
  

* Develop and deliver a multi-year surgical services strategy, including new service lines, minimally invasive and robotic techniques, and centers of excellence.
* Build referral relationships with physicians, insurers and international patient programs.
* Represent surgical services to the executive team, board and external partners.

**Required Qualifications**

* Medical degree (MD, MBBS or equivalent) from a recognized Western institution (United Kingdom, Ireland, United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand or EU).
* Completion of recognized Western specialty training with board certification or fellowship in a surgical specialty or anesthesiology, such as FRCS, FRCA, FACS, ABS or ABA certification, FRACS, FRCSC or an equivalent European board.
* Eligibility for a DHA consultant-level license (or an existing one), including a current license and Certificate of Good Standing from the home country, and successful primary source verification.

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

The role offers the opportunity to influence the quality standard for a growing federal business and help prepare the organization to support additional federal programs over time.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

  

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

  

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) facility and meaningful pharmaceutical distribution, logistics or 3PL quality exposure.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

  

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.
Direct leadership of quality teams  

  
  

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.

**Introduction**

Women’s College Hospital (WCH) is seeking a dynamic, inspiring and visionary medical leader to lead the Department of Medicine and join the medical leadership team. The Department Head will advance innovative models of specialized ambulatory care and strengthen academic, interprofessional, and interorganizational collaboration to improve access, quality and health outcomes for women and gender-diverse people.

The Department Head will report to the Hospital President & CEO through the Vice President, Medical Affairs & System Transformation and Lead Medical Executive. The Department Head is responsible for aligning the Department of Medicine’s clinical, academic and research activities with the Hospital’s strategy, in partnership with the Clinical Director for Specialized Medicine programs. The Department Head works collaboratively with the Temerty Faculty of Medicine, the Toronto Academic Health Science Network (TAHSN), partner hospitals, and the Women’s College Hospital Foundation leadership team.

**The Department of Medicine**

The Department of Medicine at WCH advances the practice and science of medicine through holistic, innovative, and interprofessional approaches to complex health conditions and distinctive models of specialized ambulatory care. The Department advances care for conditions that disproportionately affect women and special populations, including through the specialized Dermatology, Menopause and After Cancer Treatment Transition Clinics.

The Department includes approximately 150 physician faculty members, including clinician teachers, educators, quality and innovation leaders, clinician investigators and clinician scientists. Its Specialized Medicine programs bring together nursing and health discipline professionals as well as clinical and academic administrative staff.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

The Department Head will lead the clinical, academic and resource oversight of the WCH Department of Medicine. More specifically, the Department Head will:

* Provide visionary leadership and operational oversight of the Department to advance the Hospital’s strategic plan and delivery of high-quality, equitable and integrated specialized ambulatory care.
* Build and lead a team of dedicated medical professionals committed to excellence in clinical care, clinical innovation, and continuous quality improvement through physician engagement and collaborative leadership.
* Pursue excellence and represent WCH in academic medicine by advancing the educational, research and scholarly objectives of the Temerty Faculty of Medicine.
* Participate actively in WCH medical leadership.
* Grow existing and build new partnerships to advocate for and advance the goals of WCH beyond its walls.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS**

The successful candidate will be:

* A Fellow of the Royal College of Physicians of Canada or equivalent, eligible for medical licensure in Ontario, and for an academic appointment at the rank of Associate or Full Professor in the Temerty Faculty of Medicine.
* An individual with a demonstrated record of supporting others engaged in education, research and creative professional activity, in addition to having their own strong record of scholarship.
* A dynamic, compassionate and people-oriented leader, who demonstrates an empathetic, trusting, and responsive demeanor, with strong mentorship skills and a demonstrated ability to communicate strategically, engage physicians and lead change collaboratively and with accountability.
* An individual experienced in interprofessional models of care and committed to interprofessional education and patient care.
* A person with a strong commitment to social justice, equity and the health of women, gender-diverse people and equity-seeking communities, both locally and globally.
* A person with demonstrated fiscal management and resource stewardship skills, with an emphasis on linking quality outcomes with optimizing costs.

  

**EXPECTATIONS & TERM**

The successful candidate will be an outstanding academic leader and clinician, with proven excellence in managing complex health care environments. Candidates should have a deep commitment to scholarly enterprise, with experience in advancing peer-reviewed research and education in Medicine.

Salary for the role of Department Head will reflect an expected 2.5 days per week commitment, in addition to clinical compensation and other academic support based, in part, on fee-for-service billings and sessional fees.

The appointment is generally for a term of five years. After successful completion of the initial five-year appointment, a University/Hospital review will be conducted with potential reappointment for a final five-year term.
